question: A 100 W bulb is connected to a 220 V supply. The current through the bulb is approximately:
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.45 A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between **Electric Power (P)**, **Voltage (V)**, and **Electric Current (I)** is given by the formula: **P = V x I**.
 
• In this question, the **Power** of the bulb is given as **100 W** and the **Voltage** of the supply is **220 V**.
 
• To find the **Current**, the formula is rearranged as **I = P / V**.
 
• By substituting the given values: **I = 100 W / 220 V**.
 
• The calculation results in **10 / 22**, which simplifies to **5 / 11**, or approximately **0.4545 A**.
 
• Rounding to two decimal places, the current through the bulb is **0.45 A**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Power (P)**: It is the rate at which electrical energy is consumed or transferred in an electric circuit. The **SI unit** of power is the **Watt (W)**, which is equivalent to one **Joule per second**.
 
• **Electric Current (I)**: This is the rate of flow of electric charge through a conductor. The **SI unit** is the **Ampere (A)**. It is measured using a device called an **Ammeter**, which is always connected in **series** in a circuit.
 
• **Potential Difference (V)**: Also known as voltage, it is the work done to move a unit charge from one point to another. The **SI unit** is the **Volt (V)**, and it is measured using a **Voltmeter** connected in **parallel**.
 
• **Resistance (R)**: Using **Ohm's Law** and the power formula, we can also calculate the resistance of the bulb. Since **P = V² / R**, the resistance is **R = V² / P**. For a **100 W** bulb at **220 V**, the resistance is **(220 x 220) / 100**, which equals **484 Ohms**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In **India**, the standard domestic **AC supply voltage** is **220 V** with a frequency of **50 Hz**.
 
• The current calculated (**0.45 A**) represents the **RMS (Root Mean Square)** value of the current, which is typically used for **Alternating Current (AC)** ratings in household appliances.
 
• As the **Wattage** of a bulb increases while the **Voltage** remains constant, the **Current** drawn by the bulb also increases proportionally, leading to lower **Resistance**.
 
• Electric bulbs containing **Tungsten filaments** operate based on the **heating effect of electric current**, where the filament reaches high temperatures to emit light.
</ul
